transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Aurum), Ravi Singh (ML Eng, Aurum), Paula Gomez (Product, Aurum)

[00:00] Marissa: Hey everyone thanks for joining — i'm Marissa, AE on the Redwood side. quick agenda: demo quickstart flow, answer questions about hosted vs dedicated vs private, and talk credits/time-to-first-token.
[00:22] Lena: Great thanks Marissa. We're evaluating multiple vendors; primary need is customer-facing chat in our platform. want to understand how fast our engineers can get something up with redwood and what the cost/latency tradeoffs are.
[00:40] Devon: Awesome. quick note — our PLG quickstart is designed to get your devs to first token in under 10 minutes using the hosted API and SDKs. free credits spin up a sandbox org so you can hit endpoints right away.
[01:05] Ravi: That's good. Can you explain the difference between hosted and dedicated for throughput and data isolation? we also have regulators asking about audit logs and encryption.
[01:20] Devon: Sure. hosted API = fastest for dev velocity, pay-as-you-go, shared infra; dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation, SLA. private = VPC/on-prem for regulated data. all have audit logs and integrations with SAML/SSO and KMS/HSM.
[01:45] Paula: when you say 'first token in 10 minutes' — is that for local dev or full prod flow? like onboarding devs vs provisioning dedicated capacity?
[02:00] Marissa: good question. for PLG quickstart and hosted it's literally signup -> API key -> run sample and you'll see tokens streaming. dedicated takes longer because of capacity reservation and network config, usually days-weeks depending on contract and region.
[02:20] Lena: ok. can you share anything about latency numbers for a chat workload? we expect 256-token responses often.
[02:35] Devon: baseline hosted latencies for curated open models are typically 200-700ms per token depending on model size and instance. dedicated can get more predictable p95s because of reserved pools and kernel selection. note: we do automatic batching/KV cache and prefix caching so many conversational flows are cheaper and faster.
[03:05] Ravi: how about quantization — do you support q4/q8 in the runtime or is that customer-managed?
[03:18] Devon: runtime supports quantized variants and we recommend profiles per workload; our optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles and expected unit cost impact. sometimes proper kernel selection is needed — we'll share guidance.
[03:40] Lena: security — we need SOC2, ISO? and encryption both in transit and at rest. also SSO for production users.
[03:55] Marissa: yes — SOC2 and ISO are available, we have an enterprise pack with audit log retention and dedicated key management via KMS/HSM. SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC are supported. i'll send the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report link.
[04:20] Paula: any gotchas with data residency? we have EU customers and want tokens to stay in eu-west-1.
[04:32] Devon: you can pin region routing; for hosted we have region controls, dedicated and private give you more options for strict residency. we'll note this for the perf deep-dive.
[04:50] Ravi: do you have perf benchmarks for our expected seq len? we will test with 256 and a mix of short messages.
[05:02] Devon: yes — i'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and sample NVBench commands. if you want we can run a short POC on dedicated or run a hosted benchmark with your prompt set.
[05:20] Lena: our engineering lead cares a lot about cost; can you explain batching and caching effects on cost per token?
[05:33] Devon: continuous batching and prefix/KV cache reduce per-token cost. for chat, if you keep context cached and use short new input batches, unit cost drops. Redwood Optimize will give quantization/model recommendations. we'll demo cost breakdown in console next time.
[06:00] Paula: what's the developer experience like — sdk languages, examples?
[06:10] Marissa: we have SDKs for python, node, go, and examples for streaming, function calling, and embeddings. quickstart repo contains a sample chat app you can clone.
[06:25] Ravi: any friction for onboarding — do devs need a credit card? or enterprise sales involved?
[06:32] Marissa: self-serve for hosted quickstart usually just email signup + free credits; no enterprise contract required to try. dedicated/private will involve sales and contracting.
[06:45] Lena: competitors question — we've looked at openai for latency vs anthro? what makes redwood stand out?
[06:55] Devon: our angle is production-first inference with control over serving economics — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in fallbacks, and observability (per-route latency/cost). we emphasize predictable SLOs for customers using dedicated.
[07:20] Paula: are there any known issues for our stack — we're on k8s in GCP, and our infra team prefers VPC peering for private endpoints.
[07:33] Devon: we support VPC peering and private link patterns; for private/on-prem we provide a control plane that can run in your VPC. we'll share network configuration docs — note sometimes firewall rules block KV cache rolling updates if egress restricted, small gotcha.
[07:54] Ravi: ok. for the quickstart credits — how many tokens and what's the time window?
[08:02] Marissa: standard sandbox credits are $2k equivalent, 30 days, intended to run benchmarks and user flows. we can extend based on engagement.
[08:14] Lena: cool. any references or sample decks we can share internally?
[08:20] Marissa: yes i'll send the quickstart deck, quickstart repo link, security whitepaper (https://redwood-internal/docs/security.pdf) and a sandbox signup link.
[08:35] Paula: can we get a checklist for what we should bring into the perf deep-dive?
[08:42] Devon: bring sample prompt sets, target p95 latency goals, throughput targets (qps), and representative token lengths — we'll run a short benchmark live.
[08:55] Marissa: sounds good. any blockers on procurement/legal?
[09:02] Lena: procurement wants to know typical contract lengths and SLAs for dedicated.
[09:08] Marissa: dedicated is typically monthly/annual reserved capacity; SLA terms vary by package — i'll include sample contract language.
[09:18] Paula: what about rollout strategies — can we A/B between models?
[09:24] Devon: yes rollouts support canary and A/B tests and automated fallback policies to older model variants if regressions detected.
[09:35] Ravi: small nit — transcriptions sometimes garble KV-cache as KV cash, just FYI.
[09:40] Devon: ha, noted.

-- Mid-call demo snippet --
[12:00] Devon: i'll share my screen — here's the quickstart repo, you run pip install redwood, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, then run the sample chat. api call returns streaming tokens.
[12:30] Paula: i like that it's simple. do you provide a hosted playground?
[12:37] Marissa: yes sandbox console accessible via the signup link.

-- Later questions --
[24:10] Lena: licensing for private on-prem — is there an additional platform fee?
[24:18] Marissa: private has a platform fee plus support tier; i'll outline options in the follow-up.
[24:30] Ravi: how do you handle model updates for a pinned version? we need reproducible responses for compliance.
[24:40] Devon: you can pin model versions and rollout manually; we also keep model version hashes and KV cache snapshots for debugging.

[33:00] Paula: ok recap — marissa will send quickstart+credits and security docs, devon will schedule perf deep-dive and share benchmark steps, ravi will upload prompts.
[33:25] Marissa: yep that's the plan. any final Qs?
[33:30] Lena: nope, thanks. excited to try the quickstart.
[33:35] Marissa: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and SSO/security artifacts.
[33:45] Devon: i'll reach out to schedule the SE deep-dive next week.

Action items / Next steps in call: send pricing/quickstart guide, security whitepaper, sandbox credits, benchmark spreadsheet, schedule perf deep-dive.

End of transcript.
